_readme: THE inline-citation contract, in one place, read by BOTH implementations.
The answer prompt documents the citation format as bare [n] (prompts.py). The parsers are
deliberately more tolerant than that, because models emit unambiguous variants and dropping
them would render a correctly-cited answer as uncited. That tolerance is a CONTRACT, and it
is implemented twice - once per side of the wire:
Both test suites read THIS file, so the two cannot drift silently: a change on one side that
the other does not make fails that side's tests. Added 2026-08-05 after KI-35, where a third
implementation (the RG-012 gate's '\[\d+\]') diverged, scored a passing turn as FAIL, and the
false verdict was filed as an app bug. Extend the vectors here, never in one suite alone.
`expected` is the source numbers a parser must return, in order of appearance, with repeats.

vectors.name: bare lists with the three separators
out-of-range numbers still PARSE (range is the auditor's job, not the tokeniser's)
a bibtex-style key is not a citation
a bracketed phrase is not a citation
a chemical formula is not a citation
a bracketed sentence containing a number is not a citation
KI-36: number OUTSIDE the bracket, filename inside - resolves to nothing

prose with no brackets at all
